newsitem.title: GERMANY: VIAG INTERKOM ORDERS NETWORK EQUIPMENT.
newsitem.headline: VIAG INTERKOM ORDERS NETWORK EQUIPMENT.

text.p: Viag Interkom AG said on Wednesday that it had completed the initial investment phase, placing orders worth some one billion marks for network technology for its E2 mobile phone network.
The company, owned by German utility Viag AG, British Telecom and Norway's Telenor, plans to create a hybrid network that combines mobile communications and fixed-wire communications.

As part of the order, the joint venture between Canada's Northern Telecom and Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, Nortel Dasa, would deliver seven switches geared to enhance communications between mobile and fixed-wire networks.
Siemens AG would deliver fixed-wire switches, and Robert Bosch and Ericsson would deliver microwave equipment.
Nokia said it had received an order worth 300 million marks as the main contractor for base stations for the new network.
